findings.evidence: Line 129 `private theorem volume_setOf_le_ediam`; line 145 proves the bound via `ENNReal.toReal_mono`, which yields `0 ≤ diam S` vacuously if the measure were `⊤`; `densityWeightedPathLength_le` assumes no measurability of `ρ`, so for non-measurable `ρ` the LHS is the junk value `0`.
findings.fix: Make `volume_setOf_le_ediam` public (or export a `volume {s | 0 ≤ s ∧ x + s • v ∈ S} ≠ ⊤` corollary for bounded `S`, unit `v`), and add `IntegrableOn (fun s => ρ (x + s • v)) (Ici 0)` under the hypotheses of `densityWeightedPathLength_le` plus `Measurable ρ` — the proof already builds the dominating integrable indicator at lines 189–195. Point the "finite" sentences at those lemmas.
findings.issue: "In particular it is finite for a medium of compact support" (line 142) and "In particular it is finite for a bounded density of compact support" (line 177) assert nothing: `geometricPathLength` and `densityWeightedPathLength` are reals by construction (`toReal ⊤ = 0`; a divergent Bochner integral is `0`), so both inequalities hold even when the chord has infinite measure or the ray integral diverges. The only statement with the real content, `volume {s | 0 ≤ s ∧ x + s • v ∈ S} ≤ ediam S`, is `private` (line 129), and there is no integrability statement for `fun s => ρ (x + s • v)` on `Ici 0` at all — §0.3's compactly supported push-forward and its moments need both.

findings.evidence: `theorem geometricPathLength_eq_sSup (hS : Convex ℝ S) (hx : x ∈ S)` (line 226) has no norm hypothesis; for `‖v‖ = t` the value `sSup T` is the true distance divided by `t`.
findings.fix: Say "the path parameter at which the ray leaves `S`" in the `geometricPathLength_eq_sSup` docstring and in the module summary, or add the `‖v‖ = 1` qualifier where the geometric reading is asserted.
findings.issue: The docstring of `geometricPathLength_eq_sSup` (and the module docstring, lines 21–22 and 39, and the bullet at line 55) calls `sSup {s | 0 ≤ s ∧ x + s • v ∈ S}` "the distance from `x` to the boundary of the support along the ray" and `geometricPathLength` "the length of the ray … inside `S`". Both quantities are path *parameters*; they equal distance/length only for `‖v‖ = 1`, which the lemma does not assume and these lines do not state. The definition's own docstring (line 82) does carry the caveat, so the deviation is in the derived prose.

summary: The mathematics of every statement checks out, including the hard-sphere closed form and the convex sSup identification. Two docstring claims overstate what is proved: the advertised finiteness of the two functionals is carried entirely by junk-value conventions, and the "distance to the boundary" reading silently needs ‖v‖ = 1.
